New in ctsem 4

Source: NEW-IN-4.md

Version 4 adds an estimation engine written in Julia, now the default, and most new features build on it. Most code written for version 3 still runs. The tables at the end list the changed defaults and the renamed and removed functions. NEWS.md is the change log.

Julia engine

ctJuliaInstall()   # once
fit <- ctFit(data, model)

ctJuliaInstall() sets up Julia and the engine, asking before each download. The first fit after installing or updating ctsem takes a few minutes longer while the engine compiles.

  • Fits are two to three times faster than with Stan, and use multiple cores (cores).
  • New models need no compilation, so a nonlinear model starts fitting at once. With Stan, each new nonlinear model took minutes to compile.
  • backend = 'stan' fits as ctsem 3 did.

Random effects

  • Random effects are integrated with a Laplace approximation. Version 3 carried them as extra states of the Kalman filter, which underestimates individual differences in the dynamics. In linear models, random intercepts are integrated exactly. intoverpop = 'augmented' gives the old method, and ctFit() warns when that method meets nonlinear dynamics.
  • Each fit checks the approximation and warns if it affects the estimates. intoverpop = 'quadrature' then refines the fit, and ctFitUncertainty(fit, 'sample') samples the full posterior instead.
  • Random effects can be at multiple nested levels, such as people within couples: id = c('person', 'couple'), with each parameter’s indvarying naming the levels it varies at. See the multilevel vignette.
  • poprank, popunique and popblocks give the random effects covariance fewer parameters when many parameters vary.

Measurement models

Observed variables can be continuous, binary, ordinal, counts or censored, in any mix, set for each variable with manifesttype.

manifesttype type also needed
0 continuous
1 binary optional ASYMPTOTES for guessing and ceiling
2 ordinal ncategories
3 count
4 censored censormin, censormax

Nonlinear measurement and dynamics are filtered more accurately than in version 3. See the vignettes on measurement models, item response models and ordinal or continuous data.

Covariates and weights

  • Smooth effects of time independent covariates: TIpredNames = ~ s(age) + sex.
  • Subject weights, for population estimates from a sample that does not represent the population: ctFit(..., weights = w). See the sampling weights vignette.

Uncertainty and sampling

  • Standard errors come from the Hessian, as before, and each fit checks whether that approximation holds.
  • ctFitUncertainty(), which replaces ctOptimUncertainty(), computes the uncertainty by other methods, such as a sandwich estimator, the bootstrap or importance sampling.
  • ctFit(optimize = FALSE), or ctFitUncertainty(fit, 'sample') after a fit, samples the posterior until the effective sample size reaches its target. See the uncertainty vignette.

Checking and improving models

function use
ctReport(fit) run the main summaries, plots and checks, and save them to a folder
ctIdentify(data, model) see which parameters the data can inform, before fitting
ctScoreTest(fit) test whether the model is missing random effects, covariate effects or nonlinearity, without refitting (vignette)
ctFitAdequacy(fit) test the model’s one-step-ahead predictions
ctModelImprove(fit) search for a better model step by step, guided by score tests
ctLOO(fit, method = 'psis') cross validation without refitting
ctFitProfile(fit) profile likelihood
anova(), coef(), vcov(), logLik() the standard R generics

ctModelHigherOrder(), ctModelSlowComponent(), ctModelPeriodicComponent() and ctModelUniqueProcess() extend a model with second order dynamics, a slow process, a cycle, or a process specific to one indicator.

Plots

ctNetwork() and ctNetworkPlot() draw temporal and contemporaneous networks, ctPhasePortrait() a phase portrait, and ctStateDependencePlot() how a nonlinear model’s parameters change with the state. ctVarianceDecomposition() splits variance into between subject, process and measurement parts, and ctTracePlot() shows the path of the optimiser or sampler.

Model specification

  • Parameter options can be named, as in 'cint, indvarying=TRUE, tipreds=c(age)'. ctPar() writes these, and ctCov() writes covariance matrices.
  • Covariance matrices use a new parameterisation (a matrix logarithm), so their off-diagonal parameters are not correlations. summary() reports the correlation matrices (DIFFUSIONcor, T0cor, MANIFESTcor).
  • ctGenerate() simulates data from any model, including random effects and non-Gaussian indicators.

Changed defaults

ctsem 3.11 ctsem 4 for the old behaviour
backend Stan Julia backend = 'stan'
random effects when optimising Kalman filter states Laplace approximation intoverpop = 'augmented'
covariance parameterisation 'rawcorr' matrix logarithm model$covmattransform <- 'rawcorr'
cores in ctFitUncertainty(), ctFitCheckCov(), ctKalmanArray() 1 getOption('mc.cores', 2) cores = 1
cores when sampling one per chain getOption('mc.cores', 2) cores = 'maxneeded'
ACF plots quantile regression weighted spline method = 'quantile'
subjects in ctDiscretePars(), ctPredictTIP(), ctExtract(), ctKalmanArray() by position by id realid = FALSE

A fit saved with ctsem 3 and passed to ctFitUpdate() is refitted with Stan.

ctFitCovCheck() ctFitCheckCov() (old name still works)

ctModelCoverage_check() ctCoverageCheck()
ctCheckFit() ctPostPredPlots() and ctFitCheckCov()
ctFitUpdateModel(), ctStanUpdModel() ctFitUpdate()
ctGenerate(n.subjects = ) ctGenerate(n = )
ctDiscretePars(observational = ) impulseType = 'observed' or 'unit'
ctFit(iter = , chains = , control = ) sampleControl
uncertainty = 'surrogate' 'checked'
ctFit(vb = TRUE) removed
